Welcome
Head Teacher's message
Welcome to Eastover Primary School! It is with great pleasure that I welcome you to our vibrant and nurturing school community. At Eastover, we are committed to providing a safe, stimulating, and inclusive environment where every child is encouraged to thrive academically, socially, and emotionally.
We take pride in celebrating the rich diversity of our school, embracing the unique backgrounds, cultures, and experiences that each child brings. Inclusion is at the heart of everything we do — we believe that every child has the right to succeed and be heard. Through a broad and balanced curriculum, we aim to empower our pupils to become confident, respectful, and compassionate individuals who are well-prepared for the world beyond Eastover.
Please take your time to look through the website, as well as browsing on our school Facebook page. You will see various activities, events and happy children who work hard, play fair and enjoy their time at school.
If you wish to take a tour of Eastover, please make an appointment with our school office, and we will be more than happy to show you around.
We are all very proud of our school. Our Victorian buildings are full of character and set in the heart of the community. We promote success for all and take pride in all our achievements!
We look forward to working in partnership with you to provide your child with the very best educational and developmental opportunities.
Behaviour Statement
"As a school we feel it is vital to promote a caring and supportive environment in which all members of the school community feel secure & respected and which promotes good behaviour. The development of personal qualities and social skills and the fostering of socially acceptable behaviour are an integral aspect of the school curriculum."
Visions & Values
The DFE have recently reinforced the need ‘to create and enforce a clear and rigorous expectation on all schools to promote the fundamental British values of democracy, the rule of law, individual liberty and mutual respect and tolerance of those with different faiths and beliefs.’
The government set out its definition of British values in the 2011’Prevent Strategy’ and these values have been reiterated by the Prime Minister this year.
At Eastover we reinforce these values regularly and in the following ways:
Democracy is promoted through a school council, pupil questionnaires and opportunities for debate.
We promote the languages and cultural celebrations of pupils for whom English is an additional language.
The phrase ‘DISCOVER AND GROW, TOGETHER’ sums up the school values described in our 'FIVE KEY BELIEFS' it underpins our approach to everything we do, whatever the specific lesson or teaching and learning environment.
In short, ‘Discover and Grow - Together’ is a statement of intent and aspiration... and defines how we work with children.
Discover – find out, become aware of, research, investigate, search for, solve, invent.
Learning is a journey of discovery about the world around us, and discovering about ourselves. An interest in the world around us is central to this sense of discovery.
We seek to instil this sense of discovery, to enable every pupil to grow academically, emotionally and socially.

Pupil Premium & Sport Premium
The Pupil Premium was introduced in April 2011. It was allocated to children from low-income families who were known to be eligible for free school meals, and children who had been looked after continuously for more than six months. Eligibility for the Pupil Premium for 2012–13 was extended to pupils who have been eligible for free school meals at any point in the last six years (known as the Ever6 Free School Meals measure). Schools also receive funding for children who have been looked after continuously for more than six months, and a smaller amount for the children of service personnel and children adopted from care. Schools are free to spend the Pupil Premium as they see fit. However, they are accountable for how they use the additional funding to support pupils from low-income families and the other target groups.
(Ofsted: The Pupil Premium: How schools are spending the funding successfully to maximise achievement, 2013)
The Pupil Premium Grant (PPG), which is additional to main school funding, is provided to support the learning of pupils who:
The school also receives some additional funding to support children who are registered as Travellers/Gypsy-Roma.
It is for schools to decide how best to use the funding in order to help these children overcome barriers to learning and close any academic gaps with their peers.
Typical barriers to learning that may be faced by vulnerable pupils in our school include:
By knowing individual children very well, speaking with parents and drawing on research identifying effective support strategies, the school aims to use the PPG to improve the academic progress and hence future life chances of vulnerable pupils.
All children in FS, Year 1 and year 2 are entitled to receive a free school meal.
From 1 September 2026 there will be two categories of eligibility for free school meals:
Targeted eligibility: this covers children in households in receipt of Universal Credit with annual household earnings of £7,400 or less. These children will attract pupil premium.
Expanded eligibility: this covers children who are in households receiving Universal Credit with annual household earnings of more than £7,400. Children will be entitled to free school meals only. This means they will not be eligible for pupil premium.
Anyone already awarded free school meals who is attending a Somerset school will automatically be rechecked to see if they still qualify. Anyone who no longer qualifies will stop receiving free school meals from September 2026.
If you believe you may now be entitled under the new expanded eligibility criteria you can apply after 1st August 2026 using the link below:
You can apply online here: www.somerset.gov.uk/freeschoolmeals .
Useful websites and links related to the Pupil Premium:
http://www.education.gov.uk/schools/pupilsupport/premium
- All you need to know about the Pupil Premium. This is the DfE website which gives the background to the PP, effective use of the PP and also successful case studies from primary and secondary education.
http://educationendowmentfoundation.org.uk/toolkit/
- The Sutton Trust-EEF Teaching and Learning Toolkit is an accessible summary of educational research which provides guidance for teachers and schools on how to use their resources to improve the attainment of disadvantaged pupils. The Toolkit currently covers 30 topics, each summarised in terms of their average impact on attainment, the strength of the evidence supporting them and their cost.
http://www.ofsted.gov.uk/resources/pupil-premium-how-schools-are-spending-funding-successfully-maximise-achievement
- Ofsted tool kit for the PP with links to research documents including “The Pupil Premium – How schools are spending the funding successfully to maximise achievement” and “The Pupil Premium – Analysis and Challenge tools for schools”.
This strategy will be reviewed termly and reported to governors and an annual review will take place each July.

Careers
Start Small, Dream Big, Building your Future!
At Eastover Primary, we are exploring careers. This includes understanding different jobs, linking careers to the curriculum, increasing employer encounters and challenging stereotypes.
Careers Day
Foundation Stage had lots of fun in the Teddy Bear Hospital, learning about the NHS.
Year 1 and 2 had great fun learning about The National Trust and how important they are.
Sophie from Platform Rail came in to talk about the different roles within the railway as well as how to safe at a train station!
Lots of children loved their visit from Olympian Laura Gallagher and learning all about what it takes to represent our country in the Olympics.
Year 4,5 and 6 were visited by a very experienced nurse who spoke all about her long career as a nurse and within the NHS.
Year 2 were visited by Santec, the company working on the Gravity project within town where they were learning all about bridges and the importance of their strength and foundations.
UWE Engineering
Year 5 and 6 had a workshop all about engineering but also other roles that work alongside this.
Year 5 and 6 were lucky enough to speak and ask questions to a local family solicitor.
Throughout the day, the children researched and spoke about a dream job role or career they want to pursue, looking at what skills and qualifications they may need in the future to achieve this.

School Council & Art Ambassadors
Welcome to the School Council.
Every year a new council is selected by each year group via a voting system. Every pupil has the right to apply to become a member, to do this they need to put in writing why they think they are the right person to represent the school and their year group. The class then vote for who they think will best represent them and listen to the pupils at Eastover School. We meet once a week at lunch time with Miss Ashton.

Governors
Welcome to the Eastover Governors page
The Governors of Eastover Community Primary School are all committed volunteers who work to ensure each pupil at the school makes the very best progress and that the school is managed and led as effectively as possible. The governors come from a range of backgrounds but share a commitment to support and challenge the school in its work.
Governors undertake a training programme and regularly visit the school.
School governors provide strategic leadership and accountability in schools. Governors appoint the head teacher and deputy head teacher. It is governors who hold the main responsibility for finance in schools, and it is governors who work with the head teacher to make the tough decisions about balancing resources.
